record.paper_title: Some problems and conjectures about L2-invariants
record.original_question: If G is an infinite finitely generated residually finite group and G_i is a descending chain of finite-index normal subgroups with trivial intersection, must the first L2-Betti number, the cost, and the rank gradient all coincide, i.e. must b_1^{(2)}(G) = cost(G) - 1 = RG(G; (G_i))?

evidence.quote: Question 9.3 (Rank gradient, cost, and first L2 Betti number). Let G be an infinite finitely generated residually finite group. Let (Gi)i≥0 be a descending chain of normal subgroups of finite index of G with intersection {1}. Do we have b(2)1 (G) = cost(G) − 1 = RG(G; (Gi)i≥0)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be an infinite, finitely generated, residually finite group, and let $(G_i)_{i\geq 0}$ be a descending chain of finite-index normal subgroups of $G$ with $\bigcap_{i\geq 0} G_i = \{1\}$. Define:

(a) The first $L^2$-Betti number $b_1^{(2)}(G)$ of $G$, namely the von Neumann dimension $\dim_{\mathcal{N}(G)} H_1^{(2)}(G;\ell^2 G)$ of the first reduced $\ell^2$-homology of $G$.

(b) The cost $\mathrm{cost}(G)$ of $G$ in the sense of Levitt–Gaboriau: the infimum, over all essentially free measure-preserving actions of $G$ on a standard probability space and over all generating graphings $\Phi$ of the resulting orbit equivalence relation, of the total edge-measure of $\Phi$.

(c) The rank gradient with respect to the chain $(G_i)$:
$$\mathrm{RG}(G;(G_i)) := \lim_{i\to\infty} \frac{d(G_i) - 1}{[G:G_i]},$$
where $d(H)$ denotes the minimum number of generators of $H$.

Prove or disprove: for every such $G$ and every such chain $(G_i)$,
$$b_1^{(2)}(G) \;=\; \mathrm{cost}(G) - 1 \;=\; \mathrm{RG}(G;(G_i)).$$
artifact.status_search_result: The equality cost(G) − 1 = b_1^{(2)}(G) is the well-known cost-vs-L^2-Betti-number question of Gaboriau; only the inequality cost(G) − 1 ≥ b_1^{(2)}(G) is known in general. The equality RG(G;(G_i)) = b_1^{(2)}(G) is the Abért–Nikolov rank gradient problem, which remains open in general. Partial results exist (e.g., for groups with property (T) cost equals 1, matching b_1^{(2)} = 0; results of Abért–Nikolov relating rank gradient to cost of profinite completion actions), but the full triple equality is open.

status_evidence.title: Around the orbit equivalence theory, measure equivalence, cost (Gaboriau lectures)
status_evidence.snippet: Gaboriau proved cost(Γ) ≥ 1 + β_1^{(2)}(Γ); equality (fixed price / cost vs L^2-Betti) is open in general.
status_evidence.claim: The equality cost(G) − 1 = b_1^{(2)}(G) is a well-known open question of Gaboriau.

status_evidence.title: Kazhdan groups have cost 1, Inventiones math.
status_evidence.snippet: Every countably infinite group with property (T) has cost one, answering a question of Gaboriau; fixed price 1 remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress: cost is known to equal 1 for property (T) groups, consistent with b_1^{(2)} = 0.

status_evidence.title: Point processes, cost, and the growth of rank in locally compact groups
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses rank gradient, cost, and L^2-Betti numbers and their conjectured equalities.
status_evidence.claim: The relation between rank gradient and first L^2-Betti number is an active open problem (Abért–Nikolov).
